libraries
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(readxl)
library(writexl)
library(ggplot2)
library(zoo)
```

Overall is to combine the complete set of data from 09/30/2009 — 09/30/2025 (found https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/datasets/judgment-fund-report-to-congress/judgment-fund-annual-report-to-congress)
with the incomplete data from 09-30-25 to date

importing the 09/30/2009 — 09/30/2025 dataset
```{r}
data_from_09.30.2009_to_09.30.2025 <- read_csv("JudgFundRprtCongress.csv")
#parsing issues bcs some values are "null" and thus not expected character type
```
importing the incomplete data from 10/1/25- 08/31/26, from
https://fiscalcrm.my.site.com/jfpaymentsearch/s/

NB: in order to download this data you have to select certain 'search fields' (ie departments) which is unforunately inconsistent with
my effort to do all the filtering in the same place (here). 
It also produces 2 files, 1 for claims resolved through litigation and 1 for claims resolved administratively 
```{r}
admin_data_from_10.1.2025_to_08.31.2026 <- read_csv("JFPaymentAdministrativeReport_09-24-2026_122851.csv")
ligi_data_from_10.1.2025_to_08.31.2026 <- read_csv("JFPaymentLitigativeReport_09-24-2026_122844.csv")
```
okay now we have to reconcile these data sets into one giant data set. 

the first step is making sure the variables of each data set match. 
Im changing the variable names to be more usable as well. In principle, I'm mostly changing the incomplete datasets to match the complete set, except that im changing 'confirmed payment amount' to be 'payment amount' in both since some are implicitly not confirmed, and that I use this step to filter out the variable 'record date' which seems meaningless and confusing since it has little relationship with the date on which the payment was made, nor does it seem to be the date on which the lawsuit was filed. see  the judgement fund dataset dictionary for more

```{r}
data_from_09.30.2009_to_09.30.2025 <- data_from_09.30.2009_to_09.30.2025 |>
  select(judgment_type_code = `Judgment Type Code`, 
         defendent_agency_name = `Defendant Agency Name`,
         submitting_agency_name = `Submitting Agency Name`,
         control_number = `Control Number`,
         plaintiffs_counsel_name = `Plaintiffs Counsel Name`,
         payment_id_number = `Payment ID Number`,
         payment_sent_date = `Payment Sent Date`,
         payment_amount = `Confirmed Payment Amount`,
         principle_amount = `Principal Amount`,
         principle_citation_code = `Principal Citation Code`,
         principle_citation_code_description = `Principal Citation Code Description`,
         attorneys_fee_amount = `Attorneys Fee Amount`,
         attorneys_fee_citation_code = `Attorneys Fee Citation Code`,
         attorneys_fee_citation_code_description = `Attorneys Fee Citation Code Description`,
         cost_amount = `Cost Amount`,
         cost_citation_code = `Cost Citation Code`,
         cost_citation_code_description = `Cost Citation Code Description`,
         interest_amount = `Interest Amount`,
         interest_citation_code = `Interest Citation Code`,
         interest_citation_code_description = `Interest Citation Code Description`,
         source_line_number = `Source Line Number`
         )|>
  filter(payment_id_number!="null")|>
  mutate(payment_id_number = as.numeric(payment_id_number))
  

admin_data_from_10.1.2025_to_08.31.2026 <- admin_data_from_10.1.2025_to_08.31.2026 |>
  select(defendent_agency_name = `Defendant Agency Name`,
    control_number = `Control #`,
    payment_id_number = `Payment ID #`,
    payment_sent_date = `Payment Sent Date`,
    principle_amount = `Principal Amount`,
    principle_citation_code = `Principal Citation Code`,
    principle_citation_code_description = `Principal Citation Code Description`,
    attorneys_fee_amount = `Attorney Fees Amount`,
    attorneys_fee_citation_code = `Attorney Fees Citation Code`,
    attorneys_fee_citation_code_description = `Attorney Fees Citation Code Description`,
    cost_amount = `Cost Amount`,
    cost_citation_code = `Cost Citation Code`,
    cost_citation_code_description = `Cost Citation Code Description`,
    interest_amount = `Interest Amount`,
    interest_citation_code = `Interest Citation Code`,
    interest_citation_code_description = `Interest Citation Code Description`,
    payment_amount = `Payment Amount`) |>
  add_column(judgment_type_code = "Administrative")|>
  filter(payment_id_number!="null")
    
liti_data_from_10.1.2025_to_08.31.2026 <- ligi_data_from_10.1.2025_to_08.31.2026 |>
  select(defendent_agency_name = `Defendant Agency Name`,
    control_number = `Control #`,
    payment_id_number = `Payment ID #`,
    payment_sent_date = `Payment Sent Date`,
    principle_amount = `Principal Amount`,
    principle_citation_code = `Principal Citation Code`,
    principle_citation_code_description = `Principal Citation Code Description`,
    attorneys_fee_amount = `Attorney Fees Amount`,
    attorneys_fee_citation_code = `Attorney Fees Citation Code`,
    attorneys_fee_citation_code_description = `Attorney Fees Citation Code Description`,
    cost_amount = `Cost Amount`,
    cost_citation_code = `Cost Citation Code`,
    cost_citation_code_description = `Cost Citation Code Description`,
    interest_amount = `Interest Amount`,
    interest_citation_code = `Interest Citation Code`,
    interest_citation_code_description = `Interest Citation Code Description`,
    payment_amount = `Payment Amount`)|>
  add_column(judgment_type_code = "Litigative")|>
  filter(payment_id_number!="null")

```

combining the data sets into one big data set

```{r}
mega_data<-bind_rows(data_from_09.30.2009_to_09.30.2025, liti_data_from_10.1.2025_to_08.31.2026, admin_data_from_10.1.2025_to_08.31.2026)
```

lets mutate mega_data to add a column floor_date that marks the first day of the month that a claim was paid out. This will allow us-hopefully- to create graphs that count the number of claims in a given month in a given year. It's not the most elegant solution but its the only one I could find.  
```{r}
mega_data<-mega_data |>
  mutate(
    floor_date = floor_date(payment_sent_date, "month")
  )
```

Lets mutate again to add another new variable: citation_cause. This will be a simplified version of principle_citation_code, containing the information about the 'why' of the payment (eg med_mal or prop_seize) but not the how (admin or through the courts). The latter information is (with slightly less specificity) already contained in judgement_type_code_anyway
```{r}
mega_data <- mega_data |>
  mutate(
    citation_cause = case_when(
      principle_citation_code %in% c("28-USC-2677 Traffic","28-USC-2672 Traffic","28 USC 1346(b) Traffic") ~ "traffic",
      principle_citation_code %in% c("28 USC 1346(b) Fls-Arrest","28-USC-2677 Fls-Arrest","28-USC-2672 Fls-Arrest") ~ "fls_arrest",
      principle_citation_code %in% c("28-USC-2677 Med Mal","28-USC-2672 Med Mal") ~ "med_mal",
      principle_citation_code %in% c("28 USC 1346(b) Prop-Maint", "28-USC-2672 Prop-Maint","28-USC-2677 Prop-Maint") ~ "prop_maint",
      principle_citation_code %in% c("28-USC-2672  Fire-Flood") ~ "fire_flood",
      principle_citation_code %in% c("28-USC-2672 Prop-Seize", "28 USC 1346(b) Prop-Seize", "28-USC-2677 Prop-Seize") ~ "prop_seize",
      principle_citation_code %in% c("28-USC-2677 Miscellany", "28-USC-2672 Miscellany","28 USC 1346(b) Miscellany") ~ "miscellany",
      principle_citation_code %in% c("28-USC-2672 Aircrash") ~ "aircrash"
     )
  )
```



Now we create a new 'summary' dataframe where we can store some of our summary statistics
```{r}
mega_data_summary <- mega_data%>%
  group_by(floor_date) %>%
    summarize(count = n_distinct(payment_id_number), 
              payment_amount_sum = sum(payment_amount), 
              payment_amount_median = median(payment_amount),
              count_citation_code_traffic = n_distinct(payment_id_number[citation_cause=="traffic"]),
              count_citation_code_fls_arrest = n_distinct(payment_id_number[citation_cause == "fls_arrest"]),
              count_citation_code_med_mal = n_distinct(payment_id_number[citation_cause == "med_mal"]),
              count_citation_code_prop_maint = n_distinct(payment_id_number[citation_cause == "prop_maint"]),
              count_citation_code_fireflood = n_distinct(payment_id_number[citation_cause == "fire_flood"]),
              count_citation_code_prop_seize = n_distinct(payment_id_number[citation_cause == "prop_seize"]),
              count_citation_code_miscellany = n_distinct(payment_id_number[citation_cause == "miscellany"]),
              count_citation_code_aircrash = n_distinct(payment_id_number[citation_cause == "aircrash"]),
              payment_sum_citation_code_traffic = sum(payment_amount[citation_cause=="traffic"]),
              payment_sum_citation_code_fls_arrest = sum(payment_amount[citation_cause == "fls_arrest"]),
              payment_sum_citation_code_med_mal = sum(payment_amount[citation_cause == "med_mal"]),
              payment_sum_citation_code_prop_maint = sum(payment_amount[citation_cause == "prop_maint"]),
              payment_sum_citation_code_fire_flood = sum(payment_amount[citation_cause == "fire_flood"]),
              payment_sum_citation_code_prop_seize = sum(payment_amount[citation_cause == "prop_seize"]),
              payment_sum_citation_code_miscellany = sum(payment_amount[citation_cause == "miscellany"]),
              payment_sum_citation_code_aircrasht = sum(payment_amount[citation_cause == "aircrash"])
    )

```

now let's try to create some line graphs tracking changes in each of these  statistics over time
```{r}
#count of claims paid each month over time

ggplot(mega_data_summary, aes(x = floor_date, y = count)) +
  geom_line()+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 10), name = "Number of claims",
                     expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, NA))+
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_minor_breaks = "1 month", labels = scales::label_date_short())+
  theme_light()+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust=1)) +
  ggtitle("Number of successful claims per month")

#alternative look
ggplot(mega_data_summary, aes(x = floor_date, y = count)) +
  geom_point()+
  geom_smooth()+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 10), name = "Number of claims",
                     expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, NA))+
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_minor_breaks = "1 month", labels = scales::label_date_short(), name = "Year")+
  theme_light()+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust=1)) +
  ggtitle("Number of successful claims per month")

```

```{r}
# #facet wrapped histogram 
# ggplot(mega_data, aes(x=payment_amount, fill=citation_cause))+
#   geom_histogram()+
#   scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_dollar(), name = "payment amount") + #i had to scale the x axis by log in order to make anything at all visible, but it wasn't what i had in mind and i would rather not have
#   facet_wrap(~citation_cause, scales = "free_y", ncol=1)
# #this is pretty good but rstudio is making it tiny and squished for some reason

# #layered transparent density plots
# ggplot(mega_data, aes(x = payment_amount, color = citation_cause, fill = citation_cause)) +
#   scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_dollar()) + 
#   geom_density(alpha = 0.5)
# #this is pretty but close to useless

#maybe the solution is a facet wrapped density plot?
# i ended up liking this the best so I'm reducing it to just the past 10 years, getting rid of the empty 'aircrash' cause, and adding some visual elements
mega_data|>
  filter(floor_date > ymd("2016-01-01"), citation_cause!="aircrash")|>
  ggplot(aes(x=payment_amount, fill=citation_cause))+
    geom_density()+
    scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_dollar(), breaks = scales::breaks_log(n = 8), name = "Payment") + #i had to scale the x axis by log in order to make anything at all visible, but it wasn't what i had in mind and i would rather not have
    facet_wrap(~citation_cause, scales = "free_y", ncol=1)+
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 2), name = "Density", expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, NA))+
    theme_light()

#an alternative without the log scale x axis and in fact without a shared x axis at all
mega_data|>
  filter(floor_date > ymd("2016-01-01"), citation_cause!="aircrash")|>
  ggplot(aes(x=payment_amount, fill=citation_cause))+
    geom_histogram()+ # i switched to a histogram and it made me realize the density plot might be misleading...
    facet_wrap(~citation_cause, scales = "free", ncol=1)+ #scales are free bcs otherwise things are too different
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 4), name = "Payment amount", expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, NA), labels = scales::label_dollar())+
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 2), name = "Density", expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, NA))+
    theme_light()
```
